benchmark: LOAD-002 local in-process telemetry integration diagnostic

environment.external_network: socket and AxeOSConnector guards raise before product imports/route transport
environment.rss_scope: not measured; no host/container memory inference
environment.runtime_profile: local Flask test_client -> real agent blueprint/route -> DeviceRegistry -> isolated temporary SQLite

backlog.definition: queued waiting-for-handler and active HTTP dispatches are separate; admitted outstanding is their sum
backlog.scope: harness bounded queues only; not a production WSGI backlog measurement

integrity.note: SQLite row id captures receive order; chart/history use sample timestamp ordering, so late arrivals can differ from receipt sequence.

latency.percentile_method: nearest-rank: sorted[ceil(p*n)-1], clamped to valid indices
latency.units: milliseconds for summaries; raw arrays are nanoseconds from perf_counter_ns

raw_timings_ns.array_encoding: each *_json field is the complete compact JSON integer array; parse with json.loads

workload.queue_cap: 2 queued per stream (100) plus at most 50 active handlers
workload.sample_timestamps: derived from current epoch; all samples are in the past; sequence 158 arrives with a sample timestamp one second before the base while sequence 159 remains newest
workload.tenant_aliases: 50 primary streams plus 50 same-IP device rows under a second tenant
workload.worker_model: one persistent test client per worker/device stream; per-stream order serialized; all workers start on a barrier
